Ostara Naturally Dyed Eggs

Served at: Spring Equinox (Ostara)

1 dozen eggsPrep 30 minCook 15 min (plus 2-12 hours for dyeing)

Eggs are a quintessential symbol of new life, fertility, and rebirth, making them central to Spring Equinox (Ostara) celebrations. This recipe guides you through creating beautiful, naturally dyed eggs, a joyful and traditional way to welcome the spring and adorn your Ostara altar or table. These vibrant eggs represent the awakening of nature and the promise of new beginnings.

Ingredients

  • 12 large eggs
  • 4 cups (960 ml) water, plus more for dye baths
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) white vinegar, per dye bath
  • For Yellow/Orange: 2 cups (approx. 50 g) yellow onion skins
  • For Blue/Purple: 1/2 head (approx. 250 g) red cabbage, chopped
  • For Golden Yellow: 2 tablespoons (30 ml) ground turmeric
  • For Brown: 1/2 cup (120 ml) strong brewed coffee grounds or instant coffee
  • Optional: 1 teaspoon (5 ml) vegetable oil, for shine

Method

  1. Gently place eggs in a single layer in a large saucepan. Cover with at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) of cold water.
  2. Bring water to a rolling boil over high heat. Once boiling, immediately remove the pan from heat, cover, and let stand for 12-15 minutes for hard-boiled eggs.
  3. While eggs are cooking, prepare your dye baths. For each color, combine the dye ingredient (onion skins, red cabbage, turmeric, or coffee) with 2 cups (480 ml) of water and 2 tablespoons (30 ml) white vinegar in separate small saucepans.
  4. Bring each dye mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes to extract the color. Strain the solids from each dye bath, reserving the colored liquid in separate heatproof bowls or jars.
  5. Carefully transfer the hard-boiled eggs to an ice bath or run under cold water to stop the cooking process and cool them completely. This prevents a green ring around the yolk.
  6. Once eggs are cool, gently place them into the prepared dye baths. Ensure eggs are fully submerged. For deeper colors, you may need to add more dye liquid or turn the eggs periodically.
  7. Allow eggs to soak in the dye for at least 2 hours for pastel shades, or overnight in the refrigerator for more vibrant, deeper colors.
  8. Once desired color is achieved, carefully remove eggs from the dye baths using a slotted spoon and place them on a wire rack set over paper towels to dry completely.
  9. For an optional shine, once dry, gently rub each egg with a tiny amount of vegetable oil using a paper towel.

Tips

  • Experiment with other natural dyes like beet juice for pink, spinach for light green, or paprika for orange-red.
  • For speckled eggs, before dyeing, wrap eggs in onion skins or small leaves and secure with cheesecloth or an old nylon stocking.
  • Store dyed eggs in the refrigerator and consume within one week, as they are hard-boiled.
